The month, then the year

The month is the way in. The year comes after, on what the month learned.

  1. The month

    On your history and your real customers, before the year is committed.

    • Your history loaded on day one.
    • A rehearsal with your customers, before the first real message.
    • Up to ten real accounts, in the order your house sets.
    • Every order counted: resolved, corrected or held aside.
    Included in the month The report Your accounts, your product mix and who is going quiet. See it

    Paid as one month of plan. Credited against the year.

  2. The year

    Every channel and everyone in the company, on what the month learned.

    • WhatsApp, voice notes and photographs of the paper.
    • Message to delivery note, on each customer's price list.
    • Stock and catalogue, from the warehouse.
    • Delivery notes to Excel and paper, plus a read API.

    Setup sits inside the fee. Your price holds for your whole term.

The first month: Rocoto learns your business

You start on your real operation, with your customers and your history inside.

  1. Day 0Your history goes in and your WhatsApp is connectedThe last few months of orders, and the number your customers already write to.
  2. Week 1Rocoto models your business and your environment is readyYour catalogue, your price lists, your customers and your rules, on an install of your own.
  3. Week 2You test it playing your own customersYou write the way they write and watch the order come out, as many times as you like.
  4. Weeks 3–4Up to 10 real customers switched onWe recommend which ones, starting with the most important. Every order is measured: what it got right, corrections, and the times it knew to stop.
  5. Day 30The report, the month's numbers and the year's decisionWhat your own orders say about your customers and your products, with the measured month beside it. You decide the year with that in front of you.

If your environment is ready sooner, you start testing sooner.

One month, at your personalized price. We set it on the call, looking at your operation.

Questions

What happens when it gets something wrong?

It will, which is why the month is measured. Every order is counted: resolved on its own, corrected by your team, or held aside for a person to look at. That count stands before anything is committed for the year.

How is the price worked out?

It counts two things: the people who enter orders and the month's real volume. The rest of the company comes with them, at no cost. The per-order rate falls with volume, and for the first companies it is locked for twelve months. The number is settled on a call: two companies at the same volume rarely run the same operation.

What support is there?

Hours and the cutoff are agreed with your company during the month. Inside those hours, a reply the same working day, and under an hour if orders are blocked. The person who wrote the code answers, on WhatsApp. Rocoto runs on the official Meta API as a verified tech provider: your number and your Meta account stay yours, with a standard-format export whenever you ask for it. Data processing annex

Can it answer on its own?

Below the confidence threshold it flags the order rather than guessing, and that order reaches your team. Outbound messages go out when one of your people approves them.

What does it leave alone?

Invoices stay in your ERP. Your ERP stays where it is and Rocoto sits on top. Your salespeople keep the account and Rocoto keeps the typing. Accounting stays with your accountant.

Why a month before the year?

Two different questions. Your history tells you whether it is accurate on your products. The live month tells you whether your team uses it on a Tuesday when someone is off sick.

Do I have to change ERP?

No. Rocoto assembles the delivery note and your system issues the invoice. If your provider wants to integrate, we handle that with them.

Do my customers have to do anything?

They write exactly as they always have: same number, same group, same voice notes.

How many people can use it?

Everyone in the company. Pricing counts the people who enter orders; the rest come in with them.

How long does it take to start?

Days. The slow part is getting the history out of your ERP, and we handle that with your provider.

What do you need from us?

Order history, catalogue, customer list, and access to the number your customers write to. You send the exports and we load them.
